data.title: ORLEN, Carlyle sign preliminary agreement to explore energy investments
data.description:
ORLEN and Carlyle signed a non-binding memorandum of understanding to explore joint energy investments in Poland, elsewhere in the region and internationally, the companies announced Thursday. The agreement was signed at the Partnership for Transatlantic Energy Cooperation ministerial meeting in Warsaw.

For investors, the agreement signals a potential avenue for Poland's ORLEN to pursue expansion alongside an investment partner and for Carlyle to develop energy investments with an established regional operator. However, the announcement identifies no specific projects, capital commitments or financial targets, leaving the potential impact on either company’s earnings and investment spending uncertain.

The companies will assess opportunities primarily in oil and gas, renewable fuels and power generation. They intend to combine ORLEN’s operating experience and regional presence with Carlyle’s investment capabilities to develop a pipeline of potential projects.

The planned cooperation will also consider investments in industrial modernization, energy efficiency and decarbonization. The companies said their objectives include supporting European energy security and industrial competitiveness.

ORLEN Chief Executive Ireneusz Fąfara said the arrangement would help the companies evaluate large energy projects and could support ORLEN’s expansion beyond Poland. Carlyle’s chairman of energy, Marcel van Poecke, pointed to demand for reliable and affordable energy as a basis for potential investment.

Any investment would require due diligence, agreement on commercial terms, definitive documentation and internal and regulatory approvals. The companies provided no timetable for reaching an investment decision.

data.title: New York City legislation could upend Amazon's delivery model
data.description:
New York City continues its campaign to rein in delivery services and gig work with the introduction of legislation that would require last-mile delivery services to be licensed with the city and restrict the use of third-party subcontracting for deliveries.

Introduced in February of this year, NYC Intro 518, known as the Delivery Protection Act, would require companies like Amazon (AMZN), DoorDash (DASH), Instacart (CART), GrubHub, and UberEats (UBER) to obtain a license from the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and ultimately limit the use of “gig” workers.

Unlike previous NYC legislation, which focused on minimum pay and working conditions, Intro 518 would reshape the model itself and push e-commerce facilities to hire delivery drivers directly rather than rely on third-party and independent drivers.

While supporters argue that the law would protect delivery workers by making corporations like Amazon (AMZN) accountable for safety and living standards and enable employees to organize for collective bargaining, opponents warn the new law would limit a path to business ownership and eliminate a major source of income for up to 10K gig workers. 

The law could also exceed the authority of New York City, as it would impose restrictions on facilities outside the city and state.

For Amazon (AMZN), the new law would directly undermine its business model that guarantees free and fast delivery, much of which is conducted by third-party contractors.

“Right now, Amazon works with a network of small delivery businesses that are deeply embedded in your communities. If this legislation passes, we'd no longer be able to work with them, and we'd be forced to consider moving our operations outside the city. That would likely mean slower and more expensive delivery for millions of customers in New York City, while also threatening small businesses and their thousands of employees,” Amazon (AMZN) said in a blog post on its website.

data.title: Marathon Petroleum declares force majeure on North Dakota oil deliveries
data.description:
Marathon Petroleum (MPC) declared force majeure on North Dakota oil pipeline deliveries after a flurry of crude contamination issues, Bloomberg reported late Wednesday.

The line that transports Bakken crude oil has been operating intermittently since last week after operator Enbridge (ENB) saw a spike in cases of oil tainted with organic chloride, a compound that is damaging to metallurgy and can force refineries to shut down.

"Crude oil quality testing is resulting in some delays on the North Dakota pipeline system," Enbridge (ENB) said in a statement. "We are working with shippers to return the system to normal operations as quickly as possible."

The 475K bbl/day North Dakota pipeline transports oil from the Williston Basin, including the Bakken formation, to Clearbrook, Minnesota, where it flows into Enbridge's (ENB) Mainline system that hauls crude to the Midwest and Gulf Coast.

data.title: Anthropic set to dethrone SpaceX in historic IPO and rewrite top 10 largest IPO list
data.description:
Anthropic (ANT), the developer of the Claude artificial intelligence platform, has priced its initial public offering at $83 per share, raising roughly $81B and becoming the largest IPO on record.

The upsized offering of roughly 980 million shares values the company at approximately $1.5 trillion and surpasses SpaceX’s (SPCX) $75B base raise from June 2026. 

The ranking of the world’s largest IPOs by gross proceeds at pricing now stands as follows:

  1. Anthropic (ANT) (2026) — $81.3 billion
  2. SpaceX (SPCX) (2026) — $75.0 billion
  3. SK Hynix (SKHY) (2026) — $26.5 billion
  4. Saudi Aramco (ARMCO) (2019) — $25.6 billion
  5. Alibaba Group (BABA) (2014) — $21.8 billion
  6. SoftBank Corp (SFTBY) (2018) — $21.3 billion
  7. Agricultural Bank of China (ACGBY) (2010) — $19.2 billion
  8. ICBC (2006) (IDCBY) — $19.1 billion 
  9. NTT DoCoMo (1998) — $18.1 billion 
  10. Visa (V) (2008) — $17.9 billion 

These figures reflect capital raised in the primary offering and exclude concurrent private placements. The 2026 listings of Anthropic, SpaceX, and SK Hynix have reshaped the historical order previously dominated by Saudi Aramco and major Chinese and Japanese issuers. Market participants will monitor first-day trading for further indication of demand for large-scale technology offerings.

data.title: Salesforce, OpenAI, Nvidia among those picked by US to join AI export consortium
data.description:
Salesforce (CRM), OpenAI (OPENAI) and Nvidia (NVDA) were among the companies selected by the U.S. Department of Commerce to take part in its American SI Exports Program.

The program, which was created under an executive order by U.S. President Donald Trump, promotes the export of full-stack AI technologies to expand access to international markets.

"The United States is the global leader in trusted SI research, development, and innovation," said U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick. "Under the leadership of President Trump, we are extending that leadership through the Department of Commerce's American SI Exports Program. This initiative recognizes the strategic importance of America's technological leadership by expanding international markets for American innovation, strengthening our domestic industrial base, and creating more high-paying jobs for American workers." 

Other companies selected for the program include Amazon Web Services (AMZN), Cisco (CSCO), Cognizant (CTSH), Dell (DELL), HPE (HPE), IBM (IBM), Intel (INTC), Microsoft (MSFT), ServiceNow (NOW) and AMD (AMD).

"American technology leadership grows when governments and businesses around the world put it to work with trust," said Kendall Collins, president and CEO of Missionforce and Government Cloud at Salesforce. "Salesforce brings governed data, enterprise applications, and agents together to deliver faster public services, stronger operations, and greater productivity—with model choice and controls that respect customers’ sovereignty. Through the American SI Exports Program, we’re bringing American innovation and deep operational expertise to help our global partners turn intelligence into action."

The companies selected for program participation are eligible for priority government-to-government engagement, priority export control review, and priority routing for Federal financing referrals.

Other U.S. companies can apply for program participation starting on November 30 through this link.

data.title: Manchester United misses revenue estimates, reiterates FY27 outlook
data.description:
Shares of Manchester United (MANU) opened about 6.5% lower after the club reported a wider net loss for its fiscal first quarter, with revenue also coming in below analysts' expectations despite higher broadcasting income from its return to the UEFA Champions League.

Revenue for the quarter rose 4.1% year over year to £146.1 million, or about $196 million, missing the consensus estimate of $199.95 million. Adjusted basic loss per share was 7.69 pence, compared with expectations for earnings of 8 cents per share.

Adjusted EBITDA increased 2.2% to £27.5 million. The club reported an operating loss of £3 million, compared with an operating profit of £13 million a year earlier. Net loss widened to £18.1 million from £6.6 million, while adjusted net loss increased to £13.3 million from £2.6 million.

Broadcasting revenue climbed 17.7% to £35.2 million, reflecting the men's first team's participation in the Champions League, after the club had no UEFA competition in the year-earlier period. Matchday revenue increased 2.3% to £26.8 million.

Commercial revenue was nearly unchanged at £84.1 million. Sponsorship revenue declined 3% to £45.6 million, partly due to a smaller preseason tour, while retail, merchandising, apparel and product licensing revenue rose 3.5% to £38.5 million.

The operating result also reflected a smaller profit on the disposal of player registrations, which fell to £20.7 million from £45 million a year earlier. Excluding the disposal gain, the operating loss narrowed to £23.7 million from £32 million.

Manchester United (MANU) reiterated its fiscal 2027 guidance, forecasting revenue of £750 million and adjusted EBITDA of £215 million, based on the midpoints of its respective ranges.

CEO Omar Berrada said revenue remained strong and on track, while the club continued to focus on improving performances on the pitch.

Shares have gained about 30% so far this year, outperforming the broader index that rose around 7% during the same period.

Short interest on MANU stands at 5.58% of the total float.

data.title: The Fed's Jefferson discusses how different shocks affect monetary policy
data.description:
Different types of economic shocks require different responses from monetary policymakers, Federal Reserve Governor Philip Jefferson said Thursday.

One important distinction is between supply and demand shocks, he said. Typically, demand shocks can be addressed with adjusting interest rates, while supply shocks don't respond to such actions.

Also, the policymakers must consider how shocks are affecting each side of the Fed's dual mandate — price stability and maximum employment. When a shock moves the output gap and inflation in the same direction, the central bank's objectives become aligned, he noted.

"When a shock pushes them in opposite directions, there is a tradeoff," Jefferson said. "The recent rise in oil prices tied to the conflict in the Middle East is an example of the latter."

The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence represents a shock to both aggregate supply and aggregated demand with varied timing. That's a scenario that's "especially challenging for monetary policymakers," he said in prepared remarks.

"Currently, the AI buildout is exerting upward pressure on demand and inflation," Jefferson said. "In the future, advancements in productivity could exert downward pressure on inflation while continuing to support growth."

However, the Fed isn't just facing the effects of the AI buildout on inflation and the labor market.

"Energy, trade, and AI shocks are all unfolding at once," he said. "My colleagues at the Fed and my peers around the world must weigh them simultaneously. Our task is to remain attentive to our respective mandates and to keep the stance of our policies appropriately calibrated to achieve those stated goals."

Jefferson's speech did not provide his outlook for a policy path.

"For the U.S. economy, my goal is to restore price stability while maintaining a solid labor market," he concluded, according to his prepared text. "That outcome will help the economy grow according to its full potential."

data.title: Wall Street climbs as investors await Anthropic debut
data.description:
The stock market moved higher on Thursday, with technology shares leading the gains, as investors turned their attention to the highly anticipated public debut of artificial intelligence startup Anthropic.

S&P 500 (SP500) +1.1%, the Dow (DJI) +0.4%, and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) +1.9%.

Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI chatbot, is set to begin trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT after pricing its IPO at $83 a share, above its expected range. The company raised approximately $81.3 billion, and its debut could offer a gauge of how public-market investors are assessing the longer-term commercial prospects of AI amid recent weakness in several AI-linked stocks.

Meanwhile, for the week ended Nov. 14, initial jobless claims in the U.S. rose by 1K to 203K, edging past the 198K consensus, according to data released by the U.S. Department of Labor.

On the other hand, Walmart (WMT) traded lower on Thursday, despite positive results, as investors assessed the retail giant's third-quarter earnings report and outlook for the holiday quarter.
